candidate.answerReason: The permitted endpoint \(\theta=0^\circ\) has cosine 1 and sine 0. Also, the square-sum identity directly forces \(\sin^2\theta=0\).

methods.label: Identify the endpoint angle
methods.explanation: In this range, \(\cos\theta=1\) only when \(\theta=0^\circ\), and the sine is 0.
methods.levelReason: Uses the unit-circle endpoint values within the stated inclusive interval.

methods.label: Use the square-sum identity
methods.explanation:
The square-sum identity lets us find sine without first finding the angle. Since \(\cos\theta=1\),
\[\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta=1-1^2=0.\]
The only real number whose square is zero is zero, so \(\sin\theta=0\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the basic same-angle identity and the unique square root of zero.
